judgements.read_vs_write: METHOD decides, with 8 pinned read-shaped POSTs (validate_token, 3 autocompletes, 2 filtered searches, 2 view previews). Inverse trap recorded: 3 POSTs match a naive read keyword via the RESOURCE name (saved_searches, task_list_templates, task_lists) and literally say 'Creates a ...' — all writes. The 2 async export POSTs create a job resource and are writes.
judgements.stream_vs_direct_read: the 33 shipped fixture-backed streams keep their rows (greenhouse finding 21); every other read becomes a bounded direct read
judgements.binary_detection: GET-only, read from the artifact's declared success media types. Exactly 1 application/octet-stream operation. The trap here runs BACKWARDS to workday-rest's: PUT /api/v2/brands/{brand_id} declares image/jpg and image/png because the update echoes the brand logo. A 'non-JSON media type' rule alone would ship it as a download and drop the mutation.
judgements.named_dependency: three expected classes — a GET with no documented JSON success body (engine.decodeDirectReadBody + commandrunner.supportedDirectReadOutputPolicies), a write whose required record field has no scalar leaf (partial, mirroring validate.go checkCLISurfaceWriteFlags), and PUT /api/v2/users/update_many whose body is rooted at oneOf (AGENTS.md: not one executable command contract)
judgements.paging: start_time is NOT treated as paging. Every stream declares pagination type next_url over links.next / next_page / before_url, so paging is derived from response links, never a request parameter. start_time on /api/v2/incremental/* is the export's required opening watermark (400 without it). The first derivation run refused it and would have made every incremental read unreachable while naming paging as the reason; the blocklist was narrowed with the reason recorded rather than the rule weakened.
